title: Perl: eleven spatial and temporal defects live at the 5.36.3 pin

capstone-sublet.because: sublet-svheads is the Sublet heap plus Perl's SV head arena under the discipline, which is the nested allocator this corpus's defects live in.

release-differential.boundary: the release itself: every spatial or temporal memory defect live in the ported 5.36.3, whatever allocator holds the memory
release-differential.title: Eleven spatial and temporal defects live in Perl 5.36.3, each measured live at the pin and clean at master, with what each arm sees
release-differential.live_in_pin_note: Liveness is measured in both directions for every case, not inferred: each trigger reports under ASan on a build of the pin's own tree and is silent on the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master. The dates alone would not settle it -- four of the eleven fixes are DATED BEFORE the v5.36.3 tag (2023-11-28) and are still absent from it, because they landed on blead and were never backported to the 5.36 maintenance branch. Each case therefore records the ancestry that was actually checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, in both directions.
release-differential.note: The population was every commit from v5.36.3 to the master tip that touches both C source and a test (457 of 9537), filtered to the ones whose diff has the shape of a spatial or temporal memory defect and triaged by hand against the pin's sources. All eleven cases here are in scope by construction: this corpus admits only spatial and temporal memory defects, which is the study's scope, so unlike the mruby corpus it carries no null dereferences, type confusions or stack-exhaustion rows. One of the eleven is outside every arm's denominator and says so in its own file: 9e298ab597's trigger passes its own assertion on all four Capstone arms and on CheriBSD with revocation off and on, so the stale slot it needs never exists there; host ASan reports SEGV, so the defect is real but the trigger does not travel. The honest denominator is 10. 254b30e378 carried harness_limit until 2026-10-06 and that is WITHDRAWN: the defect did not execute in a domain because perl-cross installs almost none of the target library (636 pure-Perl modules absent, XSLoader.pm among them), so PerlIO_find_layer("scalar") could not require PerlIO::scalar and the open silently took the generic perlio layer. With the library staged by build-perl-domain.sh the case is caught. sysalloc-bounds is the baseline: per-object heap bounds are what applications get by default since PR #170, so a catch is a case the bounds arm does not fault on. The nested-allocator arm is sublet-svheads, and it protects ONE of Perl's nested allocators -- the SV head arena. The SV bodies, hash entries and OP slabs keep their upstream allocators, so a case whose stale pointer lives in those is out of that arm's reach by construction and its arm entry says so. FOUR arms, cumulative, each step adding exactly one thing: sysalloc-bounds is the base an application gets today (per-object heap bounds, no revocation); sysalloc-sublet protects the SYSTEM allocator spatially and temporally (the Sublet heap: bounded, every free revokes); sublet-svheads is that SAME image plus the SV head arena through the lifetime adapter, which makes it this port's analogue of the mruby port's sublet-gc; cheribsd-revocation is the same release on CheriBSD with revocation as it comes. 6, 7, 8, with CheriBSD at 7. sysalloc-sublet is the FLOOR, and it is the right floor because it catches EXACTLY the same seven cases as cheribsd-revocation -- the same set, not merely the same count, with no case unique to either. Once the system allocator is protected as well as CheriBSD protects it, the only thing left to gain is the nested allocator, and it gains exactly one case. The third arm's extra case is 17535c984a, whose SV head never returns to malloc -- invisible to ASan, to a protected system allocator, and to CheriBSD alike, which is the whole argument for protecting a nested allocator. An unprotected variant (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS=0) was also measured and is recorded in the results bundle as context rather than as an arm: it catches 6 as well, and differs only in reporting the spatial case as an untagged dereference instead of a bounds violation. CheriBSD's revocation is selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's own sshd, and every case ran under both settings so the pair controls the knob. The extra case is NOT a quarantine-timing effect: CheriBSD's shadow bitmap, read in O(1) without a sweep, shows all 2983 frees of that run quarantined and zero mallocs returning memory whose bit was still set, so the SV head never crosses the allocator boundary at all. An every-free run does make it SIGPROT and is rejected as evidence, because every-free faults on all eleven including an in-bounds read of a live object that nothing may catch.
